page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.2xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned via the KVM hypervisor. The hardware profile comprises 8 vCPUs derived from 4 dedicated physical cores with symmetric multithreading on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The CPU features 35 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, alongside architectural instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512F, and AES. Memory capacity totals 64.0 GB, establishing an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU allocation (8.0 GB per vCPU). The instance includes no local storage, requiring network-attached storage disks, and operates with a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. No hardware GPU accelerators are included.

Benchmark analysis reflects modest general-purpose compute capabilities aligned with older-generation Intel silicon. The instance registers a Geekbench single-core score of 926.0 and a multi-core score of 3518.0, placing single-core performance in the lowest 10% tier and multi-core output in the bottom 25%. Similarly, stress-ng yields 1105.78 in single-core and 5878.39 in multi-core metrics. PassMark testing produces a CPU score of 7017.84, which remains average, while memory-specific benchmarks place the memory score at 1707.14. Memory bandwidth reaches 39.24 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 34.3 GB/sec for uncached writes.

In operational and workload-oriented benchmarks, the server demonstrates targeted strengths with notable bottlenecks. Text-based workloads show weak throughput, such as gzip compression at 19.01 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 28.96 GB/sec multi-threaded. Static web serving achieves 4.51 GB/sec throughput, and Redis SET benchmark operations record 5.54 million operations per second. LLM inference remains mixed: small (135M) model inference reaches an average 99.23 tokens/sec generation, but larger 7B models yield poor throughput at 5.04 tokens/sec.

From a resource and cost efficiency standpoint, the ecs.se1ne.2xlarge provides high memory density per compute core, making it effective for footprint-heavy architectures where compute intensity is secondary. Workloads suitable for this profile include in-memory caches, staging database instances, medium-scale ETL memory buffers, and enterprise applications that require substantial memory space but do not rely heavily on raw single-thread or vector computation.
